package_info.why_malicious: The package deploys a Windows executable (WebBrowserPassView) to steal browser-stored credentials and exfiltrates them to a remote server. It was intentionally crafted to mimic legitimate packages and included code to delete evidence after exfiltration, resulting in full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon package use or install script execution)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file in the package (e.g., index.js or a script referenced in package.json)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a bundled Windows executable (WebBrowserPassView) to extract browser-stored credentials, saves the output to a file, exfiltrates the file contents to a remote server via HTTP POST, and deletes the output file to cover tracks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code launches an external executable from the package directory, reads sensitive data from a generated file, sends it to an external server, and deletes the evidence. This is highly abnormal for any npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute bundled binaries, harvest credentials, or exfiltrate data. Normal behavior would be limited to package functionality, not credential theft.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate developer tools may execute binaries for build or test automation, but never for credential extraction or exfiltration.
key_indicators: Execution of external binary via child_process
HTTP POST to hardcoded external server

attack_chain.action: User installs or runs the bb-builder package, triggering the malicious script.
Malicious script executes WebBrowserPassView to extract browser credentials and writes them to a file.
Script reads the credentials file and sends its contents to a remote attacker-controlled server via HTTP POST.
Script deletes the credentials file to remove evidence of the theft.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of bundled Windows credential recovery tools (e.g., WebBrowserPassView) from npm package directories
Unexpected child_process.exec calls referencing .exe files in node_modules
Immediate network POST requests to external, non-standard domains after file creation
Deletion of files immediately after network exfiltration
file_indicators: Temporary files such as out.html created and deleted in quick succession
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that bundle and execute Windows PE files, especially credential recovery tools. Flag any child_process executions of .exe files within node_modules. Detect HTTP POST requests to suspicious or hardcoded external domains immediately following file creation. Alert on rapid file deletion patterns after network activity. Review package.json scripts for unexpected install or postinstall hooks.
